ratings.reviewer_notes: Review identifies TGF-beta and Th2 cytokines IL-5 and IL-13 as mediators of airway remodeling, but does not specifically connect exacerbations to remodeling.

In an OVA mouse model, inhibition of TGF-beta1/Smad2 and IL-17A signaling coincided with fewer asthma-attack symptoms and improved remodeling, but an exacerbation-to-remodeling mechanism was not specifically tested.
Directly tests IL-17 blockade in LPS-exacerbated allergic airway inflammation and demonstrates reduced TGF-beta, matrix-remodeling markers, collagen, and other airway-remodeling outcomes.
Shows that treatment concurrently reduces IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-17, TGF-beta and extracellular-matrix remodeling in chronic allergic inflammation, but lacks an asthma-exacerbation model.
Provides the exacerbation side of the mechanism, implicating IL-5, GM-CSF, CXCL10, IL-8 and Th2 cytokines in eosinophilic or neutrophilic exacerbations, but does not evaluate airway remodeling.
Human biopsy study links IL-17F, and more broadly Th17 cytokines, to frequent exacerbations and neutrophilic severe asthma, but does not assess remodeling outcomes.
Direct intervention study in LPS-exacerbated asthma shows that IL-17 inhibition attenuates bronchial vascular remodeling, TGF-beta and multiple matrix-remodeling markers.
ACO mouse study jointly measures cytokines including IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-17 and TGF-beta with collagen remodeling, but uses asthma-COPD overlap rather than asthma exacerbation.

Review directly identifies IL-4 and especially IL-13 as drivers of structural airway remodeling and discusses how targeting them reduces severe-asthma exacerbations, while noting uncertain reversal of established remodeling.
Focused review of TGF-beta and IL-13 in allergic airway remodeling, including context-dependent mechanistic evidence, but it does not specifically address exacerbations.
Describes IL-13 as an effector linking persistent Th2 inflammation to TGF-beta activation, fibrosis and disease progression, but not specifically exacerbation-driven remodeling.
Human bronchial-biopsy evidence associates active TGF-beta/Smad2 signaling with basement-membrane thickening, supporting TGF-beta in remodeling but providing no exacerbation data.
